title: Where are the arms and the vertex in a compass?
description: A compass is opened by turning its two legs apart. The two legs are drawn as rays, and the point where they are joined is found. Keeko's doubt, that the pointed tips are the vertex, is broken by the tips that move to a new place while the joint stays still.
teaching_notes: One idea: the parts that turn are the arms, and the joint they turn about is the vertex. Watch for students who pick the sharp tips as the vertex.

source: In a compass or divider, we turn the arms to form an angle. The vertex is the point where the two arms are joined. Identify the arms and vertex of the angle.
video_script.why: The child finds the arms and the vertex of the angle that a compass makes when its legs are turned.
video_script.substitution: Draw each leg of the compass as a ray that starts at the joint.
video_script.anchor: a compass or divider whose two legs are turned apart to form an angle
video_script.wrong_answer: the pointed tips are the vertex
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the pointed tips are the vertex because they are the sharp parts. The tips are shown in three different places while the joint stays at one place, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The legs are the arms, and the vertex is the joint at the top

final_answer.value: The two legs of the compass are the arms, and the vertex is the joint at the top where the arms are joined
final_answer.spoken: the two legs of the compass are the arms, and the vertex is the joint at the top where the arms are joined

never_show: the joint named as the vertex, before the answer beat
maths_rules: An angle is formed by two rays with a common starting point; the rays are the arms and the starting point is the vertex.
In a compass the two legs turn, so each leg lies along an arm.
The vertex is the point where the two arms are joined, so it is the joint at the top of the compass.
Slip: the pointed tips move when the legs turn, so a tip is not the vertex.
video_script.design: One idea: the legs are the arms and the joint they turn about is the vertex. The compass stays on the board and opens wider and narrower. The wrong idea is that the pointed tips are the vertex.
